questions.question_text: An L-shaped prism has a cross-section made of a bottom rectangle $12$ cm by $2$ cm and an upright column $4$ cm wide reaching a total height of $7$ cm. The prism is $5$ cm long. Find its volume.

options.why: Used the full $12\times 7$ rectangle for the cross-section instead of dissecting the L-shape.
Found the cross-sectional area $44$ cm² but forgot to multiply by the $5$ cm length.
Used the full $7$ cm height for the column instead of subtracting the $2$ cm foot, giving column area $4\times 7$.

questions.question_text: The end of a shed is a pentagon: a $10$ m by $4$ m rectangle with a triangular roof of base $10$ m and height $3$ m on top. The shed is $6$ m long with this uniform cross-section. Find its volume.

options.why: Forgot the $\tfrac12$ on the triangle, using $10\times 3$ for the roof instead of $\tfrac{10\times 3}{2}$.
Found the cross-sectional area $55$ m² but did not multiply by the $6$ m length.
Left out the triangular roof entirely and used only the $10\times 4$ rectangle.

questions.question_text: A T-shaped beam has a cross-section with a top bar $10$ cm wide and $2$ cm thick, and a stem $3$ cm wide and $6$ cm tall below it. The beam is $8$ cm long. Find its volume.

options.why: Found the cross-sectional area $38$ cm² but forgot to multiply by the $8$ cm length.
Treated the cross-section as one $10\times 8$ rectangle rather than a T made of a bar and a stem.
Used only the top bar $10\times 2$ and ignored the stem before multiplying by $8$.

questions.question_text: A concrete edging is a prism whose cross-section is a trapezium with parallel sides $8$ cm and $5$ cm and a perpendicular height of $6$ cm. The prism is $20$ cm long. Find its volume.

options.why: Averaged nothing and used $8\times 6$ as the area, treating the trapezium as a rectangle of the longer side.
Forgot the $\div 2$ in the trapezium formula, using $6(8+5)$ for the area.
Found the cross-sectional area $39$ cm² but did not multiply by the $20$ cm length.

questions.question_text: A prism has a right-angled cross-section like a ramp: it can be split into a $5$ cm by $6$ cm rectangle with a right-angled triangle of base $5$ cm and height $4$ cm on top. The prism is $9$ cm wide. Find its volume.

options.why: Forgot the $\tfrac12$ on the triangle, using $5\times 4$ for the triangular part.
Used only the $5\times 6$ rectangle and left out the triangle on top.
Found the cross-sectional area $40$ cm² but did not multiply by the $9$ cm width.

questions.question_text: A block is a prism formed from a $12$ cm by $8$ cm rectangle with a $5$ cm by $3$ cm rectangular notch cut out of it. The prism is $4$ cm long. Find the volume of solid material.

options.why: Used only the full $12\times 8$ rectangle and forgot to subtract the notch.
Added the notch area instead of subtracting it, giving $111\times 4$.
Found the cross-sectional area $81$ cm² but did not multiply by the $4$ cm length.

questions.question_text: An L-shaped prism has a cross-sectional area of $54$ cm² and a volume of $486$ cm³. Find the length of the prism.

options.why: Multiplied $54$ by $10$ instead of dividing $486$ by $54$ to undo $V = Ah$.
Divided $54$ by $486$, inverting the correct $486 \div 54$.
Subtracted $54$ from $486$ instead of dividing to find the length.

questions.question_text: Prism P has a house-shaped cross-section: a $6$ m by $5$ m rectangle with a triangle of base $6$ m and height $4$ m on top, and it is $10$ m long. Prism Q is a trapezoidal prism with cross-sectional area $40$ m² and length $9$ m. Which prism has the greater volume, and by how much?

options.why: Reversed which is larger: $P=420$ m³ exceeds $Q=360$ m³, not the other way round.
Forgot the $\tfrac12$ on P's triangle, inflating P to $510$ m³ before comparing.
Assumed equal areas give equal volumes, ignoring the different cross-sectional areas and lengths.

questions.solution_text:
Prism P: $A = (6 \times 5) + \frac{6 \times 4}{2}$
$= 30 + 12$
$= 42\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = 42 \times 10$
$= 420\text{ m}^{3}$
Prism Q: $V = 40 \times 9$
$= 360\text{ m}^{3}$
$420 - 360 = 60$
Prism P is greater, by $60$ m³.

questions.question_text: A prism has a cross-section made of a $10$ cm wide rectangle of unknown height with a triangle of base $10$ cm and height $4$ cm on top. The prism is $6$ cm long and has a volume $780$ cm³. Find the height of the rectangle.

options.why: Forgot to subtract the $20$ cm² triangle before dividing, using $130 = 10x$.
Subtracted the full $10\times 4 = 40$ instead of the triangle's $20$ before dividing.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area $130$ cm² and read it off as the height.

questions.solution_text:
$A = \frac{V}{h}$
$= \frac{780}{6}$
$= 130\text{ cm}^{2}$
Let the rectangle height be $x$.
$130 = 10x + \frac{10 \times 4}{2}$
$130 = 10x + 20$
$10x = 110$
$x = 11\text{ cm}$
